blocks.text: The depot report organises work as recurring, location-level operations: shift leads check key areas each morning, drivers collect routes and scan parcels, and supervisors summarise delays weekly. Each city report follows this pattern, alongside a local change or constraint such as staffing, equipment, or weather. [P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7, P8]

The release process instead organises work around release gates and named stage owners: Alice owns Build and Bob owns Deploy. Build includes compiling sources and running unit tests; Deploy restarts workers one at a time. [P9, P10, P11, P12]

They agree in presenting work as structured steps with responsibilities attached, but at different levels: the depot report describes recurring operational duties across teams, while the release process assigns owners to release stages. The depot report does not describe build or deployment stages; the release process does not describe depot staffing, parcel handling, or delay reporting. [P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7, P8, P9, P10, P11, P12]

evidence_gaps: The release process says there are three gates, but the supplied passages do not identify or describe a third gate.
